To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the gender effect was significant for both GEFT and MR; 2) the GEFT and MR scores were positively related to the anatomy examination results; 3) the best students had the highest scores on the MRT and the Gordon Test of Visual imagery control; 4) the best students were the ones who spent more time in the learning session.
visuo-spatial and MR abilities are important factors in the learning of anatomy, and that the best students are those who have a high level of MR ability and a high level of visuo-spatial ability.
visuo-spatial abilities, mental rotation and functional anatomy are correlated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of spatial representation and MR in the learning process.
the relationship between visuospatial representation, mental rotations and functional anatomy learning.

the importance of MR ability in anatomy learning, and it is a first step in the direction of a better understanding of visuo-spatial abilities, and their relationship to the acquisition of anatomically related skills.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

visuo-spatial abilities and mental rotation abilities are important in the learning of anatomy and that the use of tests of visuo-spatial and mental rotation abilities in the learning of the human body is useful and can be recommended.
visuo-spatial abilities, MR ability and time spent on personal study are important predictors of success in anatomy learning.
the visuo-spatial abilities and MR abilities are important for anatomy learning, and the best students in anatomy are those who are better at MR and have higher visuo-spatial skills.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
students with higher spatial abilities and mental rotation ability are better at anatomy.
the visuo-spatial abilities and the MR abilities may be considered reliable predictors of success in learning functional anatomy.
the use of visuo-spatial and mental rotation tests in anatomy teaching may be helpful in improving students’ performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
visuo-spatial and MR abilities may be useful in the learning of functional anatomy.
students with better visuo-spatial and MR abilities are able to learn anatomy better than those with lower abilities.
the use of tests to evaluate visuo-spatial abilities may be useful for the identification of students who are at risk of failing in the learning process.
